request: the owner, 2026-10-02 (relayed by the orchestrating session): "the southern map is empty ... the south needs places, not just creatures. Somewhere to find, something in it. The mansion and the Ursaluna cave are the model." The unit: a place to find on Sunset Isle, built round Codex's resident the Orchard Sleeper (data/resident_encounters.json orchard_sleeper, a level 60 Slaking at (2816, 7080), build_brief 'Sunset Isle failed orchard: 6-10 storm-bent trees, overgrown rows, windfall and collapsed shed; trigger 18, leash 26'). This place IS that orchard; the Slaking itself is placed by another builder and nothing here writes near it.
ground_rule: Every Y is computed by tools/old_orchard.py from tools/ground.py (the canonical heightmap, rounded). Nothing in this file is a Y. A tree stands on its own column's ground + 1; the press-house floor on max(ground under its walls) + 1 (tools/lopunny_house.py's convention); each garden-wall column, hive stand and lantern post on its own ground + 1; the cellar hangs from the house floor.

site.measured: 2026-10-02 from tools/ground.py (the canonical heightmap, the water export land_8k_16_rescaled_b145_pads_rift_water.png). The resident's anchor (2816, 7080) reads y66 (data/resident_encounters.json measured 65.8): DRY, 4 above sea level y62; the sea is about 40 blocks north-east of it. The ground falls north-east to the strait shore in a gentle bench: y64-66 at the anchor, y65 everywhere under the press-house (13 by 13, range 0), y66-79 across the rows (x2736-2796, z7062-7106), y65-67 under the kitchen garden. Sub-region sunset_east (data/regions.json polygon), tier 8, band 43-53 (data/spawns.json subregions sunset_east).
site.neighbours: Nothing in data/placements.json, data/towns.json, data/landmarks.json, data/route_paths.json, data/rivers.json or any other site file lies within 450 blocks of the anchor but these (measured 2026-10-02 over every data/*.json coordinate): the themed palm sapling sapling_palm_sunset_east at (2840, 7080) with its three nest Habitat Blocks (y77, y100, y129) 24 blocks east of the anchor, its five young companion palms and its sand dressing (keep_out below); and the Sunset isle's ferry landing (data/ferries.json sunset_isle_landing, (2575, 6899)), 300 blocks north-west. Sunset West (data/towns.json) is on the mainland shore across the strait. No route leg crosses the isle (off the critical path by construction).
site.findable: From the isle's ferry landing (2575, 6899): walk the north shore east-south-east about 230 blocks to the press-house. The beacon is the giant palm sapling_palm_sunset_east (a 51 by 71 by 49 template, crown to about y134) standing at the east end of the rows, its crown directly over the sleeper (its nearest leaves at y115 above the anchor; none of its blocks at the Slaking's height within 4 of the anchor, and none west of x2809). Measured 2026-10-02 (tools/old_orchard.py plan): from the landing's arrival spot at eye height the straight line to the palm's crown (321 blocks) clears the heightmap by at least 3.1 blocks, and to the press-house ridge y79 (262 blocks) by at least 2.7; trees and other foliage are NOT counted, so the ridge may be hidden and the palm is the mark. From the Sunset strait ferry's line (data/ferries.json sunset_strait, south pier (2701, 6639) to the landing) the palm is about 250 blocks south-east over open water.

bounding_boxes.why: every column this pack writes or clears, for the integrator's collision check with the other builders' places
the hives, the drying racks, the gate and door posts and the track's spur from the press door

site.bounding_boxes_rule: every write and every clear lies in old_orchard_all and in at least one of the other boxes (tools/old_orchard_audit.py footprint)

resident.why: the common brief of 2026-10-02: no block within 4 blocks of a resident's anchor column and never the ground under it; another builder is placing the Slaking there. The pack's writes all lie west of x2805, at least 11 blocks from the anchor, and the audit checks every one against data/resident_encounters.json directly (not this copy). Its trigger (18) and leash (26) are read from the resident's build_brief by the audit: the keeper, the press-house door, the cellar and the Habitat Block's spawn box all lie outside the leash, so talking to the keeper and taking the find never wake him; the east end of the rows lies inside the trigger, so walking the last trees does.

keep_out.basis: tools/themed_saplings.py place() and setting() on data/themed_saplings.json sapling_palm_sunset_east, computed 2026-10-02 (the template boxes, not the leaves: conservative). tests/test_old_orchard.py recomputes them from that tool and fails if they move.

blocks.rule: vanilla 1.21.1 only. No chests (tools/portals_audit.py records a chest as a Gimmighoul condition) and no beds (the blackout's checkpoints own respawn points). The one spawn condition written is minecraft:oak_leaves (spawn_conditions_allowed), which data/spawn_block_policy.json allows for foliage objects, gardens and orchards: an orchard is made of it. No pumpkin (Gourgeist), no wheat (Elgyem), no cobweb (Ariados), no flowering azalea (Combee): all measured against data/spawn_blocks.json.

spawn_conditions_allowed.minecraft:oak_leaves: Cobblemon 1.8.0's own Applin, Flapple and Appletun spawns name oak_leaves in neededNearbyBlocks (data/spawn_blocks.json). The wilderness keeps the default pools (data/spawns.json philosophy), so the rows may draw the default low-level Applin (1-26) as any oak wood anywhere does; the orchard's own Applin come from its Habitat Block at the isle's band. data/spawn_block_policy.json's leaves entry allows it for foliage objects, gardens and landmark trees.

orchard.layout_why: five rows of eight on an 8-block grid, running east-west down the bench towards the sea and the giant palm. The middle alley (z7080) is left wide for the old cart track, and it points straight at the sleeper: the Slaking lies where the track runs out, 22 blocks past the last tree, under the palm. The east end is the windward end: the storm-bent and fallen trees are there, and the windfall he came for.

tree.why: a pruned fruit tree gone wild: a 3-log trunk, a crown of persistent oak leaves 5 wide at its two lowest courses and 3 wide above, ragged at the corners, and leaves let down to the trunk's second log on the overgrown ones. Persistent, so a crown never decays whatever is cut near it.

variants.why: [z, x] per tree. stump: felled long ago, one log left. dead: a bare trunk 4 high with one stub branch. fallen: the windfall, a stump and its trunk lying east along the row towards the sleeper. bent: storm-bent, the trunk stepping one block north-east at its top and the crown with it. Eight bent (the resident's brief: 6-10), all at the windward east end. Every other tree is alive.

track.why: the cart track, dirt path every second column (the rest grassed over), from the press-house door south to the middle alley and along it east. It stops at x2805, eleven blocks short of the sleeper.

overgrowth.why: the alleys gone to grass: about one column in three of the rows' box (outside the track, the trees and every other feature) gets a grass block and a plant on it, picked by a fixed hash of the column so a rebuild writes the same ones. Single-block plants only: a two-block tall grass set by command loses its lower half to the first neighbour update that finds the upper missing.

press_house.why: a stone cider press-house, 13 by 13 outside, on the one dead-flat 13 by 13 bench of the site (heightmap y65 under every wall). Cobblestone and mossy cobblestone walls with stone-brick quoins, 5 high, under an oak gable whose ridge runs east-west. The storm took the east half of the roof: west of lx 1 it stands; east of it only the north eaves, two bare rafters and the rubble on the floor. The press stands in the open half: two posts, a beam, the screw and the cauldron it pressed into. The intact west half keeps the casks, a lantern on a chain, and in its north-west corner the trapdoor to the cellar.
press_house.distance_to_anchor_why: the house's centre is 41 blocks from the anchor and its nearest corner 31: outside the leash (26)

cellar.why: the press cellar: a 7 by 7 room, 3 of air, under the intact half of the floor and centred under the house. Its ceiling is the block under the house floor, its floor 5 below the house floor (y61, under sea level, but sealed: every block of the room's walls, floor and ceiling is written solid, and under_fill rows of stone under the floor). Reached only by a ladder from the trapdoor. Casks on the walls; the find is the barrel in the south-east corner (data/rewards.json old_orchard_cellar).

kitchen_garden.why: the walled kitchen garden west of the press: a cobblestone wall (mossy where the damp got in) one high on each column's own ground, a gate on the east side facing the press. Inside, beds of coarse dirt gone to sweet berry bushes, a melon bed run wild, a rooted-dirt path, a composter and a rain cauldron.

beehives.why: four hives on log stands along the north edge of the rows, where the keeper's bees worked the blossom. Empty boxes now (a hive set by command holds no bees); vanilla beehives, honey_level 5, no spawn condition.

drying_racks.why: two racks between the garden and the press: fence posts at the ends, a course of closed trapdoors laid on top as slats, hay under them. Fruit was dried here for the winter.

lantern_posts.why: lit as a town (docs/STATE.md 'Places are lit as towns'): a lantern on two oak fence posts at the press door and the garden gate, and a staggered lattice through the alleys, 16 apart along each alley and offset 8 from the next (x2790 moved to x2792 to keep the track's spur clear). Lanterns, never light blocks. The cellar and the house each hang their own. Measured 2026-10-02 with block light taken as 15 less the Manhattan distance from the nearest lantern, leaves not counted: 4,642 of the 5,012 ground columns in the feature boxes are lit; the 370 dark ones are the press-house's north corners on the shore side and the rows' westernmost margin. Not dark by design: the keeper has come back and lit the way.

applin.why: an ACTIVATED Habitat Block (data/habitat_blocks.json, placed by tools/habitat_blocks.py with every other block, R9E) in the trunk of a living tree in the west half of the rows, disguised as its own log (the sapling nests' pattern: tools/themed_saplings.py), on a Habitat pool authored in data/spawns.json: Applin, with Tropius, and the two apple evolutions rare. The orchard's fruit walks. This pack writes the trunk the block sits in, so it runs BEFORE R9E.
applin.slakoth_finding: The brief proposed Slakoth and Vigoroth. Measured against the rules they cannot spawn here: sunset_east is tier 8, band 43-53 (data/encounter_design.json, data/spawns.json), and the evolution policy (data/spawns.json evolution_policy: a stage spawns from its own evolution level or the band's floor up to four past its next level evolution) gives Slakoth (evolves at 18, Cobblemon 1.8.0 slakoth.json) the range 43-22 and Vigoroth (evolves at 36) 43-40: both empty. A wild Slaking pool would make the resident one of many. The pool is the orchard's own fruit instead.

npc.why: Wenna Marlow, the orchard's last keeper, back on the ferry from the mainland: she stands beside the spur of the cart track two blocks south-west of the press-house door, on her column's ground + 1, facing the rows. 36 blocks from the anchor, outside the leash, so her conversation never wakes the sleeper. Placed over RCON by spawnnpcat after a restart (tools/reapply.py's "npc" action, step R18SO after R17N, as R18U places the den's watcher); the class ships in cobblers_dialogue, compiled from data/dialogue.json. Her talk points at the cellar.

find.why: a cache (data/rewards.json, ADR-002): reaching the cellar's south-east corner grants it once per player; the barrel is scenery. Leftovers (the keeper's father's 'best', for a long winter: late-game, a held item worth the ferry) and the two apples that evolve the orchard's Applin (a Tart Apple to Flapple, a Sweet Apple to Appletun: Cobblemon 1.8.0 applin.json item_interact evolutions).

access.ferry: data/ferries.json sunset_strait: Sunset West's south pier to sunset_isle_landing (built 2026-09-30 by tools/ferry_docks.py), $100 each way. The isle's swim crossing is a gate (255 blocks of strait). No jetty is added here: the isle already has its landing, 230 blocks from the press-house along the north shore.
access.walk: from the landing east-south-east along the shore bench (y63-70), no climb; the giant palm is the mark.
